     6	/// The purposes we take consent for, one per processing activity.
     7	///
     8	/// Deliberately narrow. NJDPA excludes "acceptance of a general or broad terms
     9	/// of use" from what counts as consent, and the FTC's X-Mode/InMarket orders
    10	/// make location consent purpose-scoped — consent for proximity matching does
    11	/// not stretch to anything else. Adding a use means adding a purpose here and
    12	/// asking again, not quietly reusing an existing grant.
    13	enum ConsentPurpose {
    14	  /// Gender + sexual orientation. Special-category data under GDPR Art. 9 and
    15	  /// "sensitive data" under NJDPA, CT, MD and others.
    16	  sensitiveProfile('sensitive_profile'),
    17	
    18	  /// GPS upload for proximity matching.
    19	  preciseLocation('precise_location'),
    20	
    21	  /// Collection while the app is closed.
    22	  backgroundLocation('background_location'),
    23	
    24	  /// BLE scan/advertise and the encounter records it produces.
    25	  bleProximity('ble_proximity'),
    26	
    27	  /// Profile photo storage and verification.
    28	  photoProcessing('photo_processing');
    29	
    30	  const ConsentPurpose(this.wire);
    31	
    32	  /// The value stored server-side. Must match the CHECK constraint in 0039.
    33	  final String wire;
    34	}
    35	
    36	/// Records and revokes unbundled, purpose-scoped consent.
    37	///
    38	/// The client never writes `consent_records` directly — it has SELECT only, so
    39	/// the audit trail cannot be forged. Everything goes through the RPCs.
    40	class ConsentService {
    41	  const ConsentService();
    42	
    43	  /// Bump when the privacy policy changes materially. Stored per grant so a
    44	  /// policy change can invalidate prior consent and force a re-ask.
    45	  ///
    46	  /// TODO: move to AppConfig once counsel has settled the actual policy text
    47	  /// and its versioning scheme.
    48	  static const String policyVersion = '2026-07-20';
    49	
    50	  /// Whether consent can be recorded at all (real backend + signed in).
    51	  /// Callers that gate features on consent skip the gate when this is false —
    52	  /// there is no server to record against, and nothing leaves the device.
    53	  bool get ready => _ready;
    54	
    55	  /// Never throws: AppConfig reads dotenv, which is not initialised in every
    56	  /// context (tests, early boot). A consent screen must still render.
    57	  bool get _ready {
    58	    try {
    59	      return AppConfig.hasRealSupabase &&
    60	          InRangeSupabase.clientOrNull?.auth.currentUser != null;
    61	    } catch (_) {
    62	      return false;
    63	    }
    64	  }
    65	
    66	  /// Records consent for one purpose. Idempotent — re-granting an active
    67	  /// consent does not restamp the original moment, which is the fact we have
    68	  /// to be able to evidence later.
    69	  ///
    70	  /// [uiSurface] identifies where it was taken (e.g. 'onboarding.consent_step')
    71	  /// and lands in the audit trail.
    72	  Future<void> grant(ConsentPurpose purpose,
    73	      {required String uiSurface}) async {
    74	    if (!_ready) return;
    75	    await InRangeSupabase.client.rpc('grant_consent', params: {
    76	      'p_purpose': purpose.wire,
    77	      'p_policy_version': policyVersion,
    78	      'p_ui_surface': uiSurface,
    79	    });
    80	  }
    81	
    82	  /// Withdraws consent. Must stay exactly as easy to reach as granting
    83	  /// (GDPR Art. 7(3)); NJDPA allows 15 days to take effect, the server takes
    84	  /// effect immediately and deletes location data for location purposes.
    85	  Future<bool> withdraw(ConsentPurpose purpose) async {
    86	    if (!_ready) return false;
    87	    final result = await InRangeSupabase.client
    88	        .rpc('withdraw_consent', params: {'p_purpose': purpose.wire});
    89	    return result == true;
    90	  }
    91	
    92	  /// Current state for every purpose, for the consent screen and for answering
    93	  /// "what did I agree to?".
    94	  Future<Map<ConsentPurpose, bool>> current() async {
    95	    if (!_ready) return const {};
    96	    try {
    97	      final rows = await InRangeSupabase.client.rpc('my_consents') as List;
    98	      final byWire = {for (final p in ConsentPurpose.values) p.wire: p};
    99	      final out = <ConsentPurpose, bool>{};
   100	      for (final row in rows.cast<Map<String, dynamic>>()) {
   101	        final purpose = byWire[row['purpose'] as String?];
   102	        // Rows are ordered newest-first per purpose, so the first one wins.
   103	        if (purpose != null && !out.containsKey(purpose)) {
   104	          out[purpose] = row['granted'] == true;
   105	        }
   106	      }
   107	      return out;
   108	    } catch (e) {
   109	      debugPrint('ConsentService.current failed: $e');
   110	      return const {};
   111	    }
   112	  }
   113	}
   165	    } catch (e) {
   166	      debugPrint('ConsentScreen: could not load consent state: $e');
   167	      current = const {};
   168	    }
   169	    if (!mounted) return;
   170	    setState(() {
   171	      _state
   172	        ..clear()
   173	        ..addAll(current);
   174	      _loading = false;
   175	    });
   176	  }
   177	
   178	  bool _granted(ConsentPurpose p) => _state[p] ?? false;
   179	
   180	  bool get _requiredSatisfied =>
   181	      _items.where((i) => i.required_).every((i) => _granted(i.purpose));
   182	
   183	  /// In manage mode each toggle applies immediately — withdrawal should not be
   184	  /// gated behind a save button that granting did not require.
   185	  Future<void> _toggle(_Item item, bool value) async {
   186	    setState(() {
   187	      _state[item.purpose] = value;
   188	      _error = null;
   189	    });
   190	    if (!widget.manage) return;
   191	    try {
   192	      if (value) {
   193	        await _service.grant(item.purpose, uiSurface: _surface);
   194	      } else {
   195	        await _service.withdraw(item.purpose);
   196	        // Withdrawal must stop the processing on this device too, not just
   197	        // record a preference on the server.
   198	        if (item.purpose == ConsentPurpose.bleProximity &&
   199	            ref.read(beaconControllerProvider).isOn) {
   200	          await ref.read(beaconControllerProvider.notifier).toggle();
   201	        }
   202	        if (item.purpose == ConsentPurpose.photoProcessing) {
   203	          // The server wiped the photo references; drop cached URLs so the
   204	          // UI stops showing them.
   205	          PhotoUrlService.clearCache();
   206	        }
   207	      }
   208	    } catch (e) {
   209	      if (!mounted) return;
   210	      setState(() {
   211	        _state[item.purpose] = !value; // roll back the visual state
   212	        _error = 'Could not update that setting. Please try again.';
   213	      });
   214	    }
   215	  }
   216	
   217	  Future<void> _submit() async {
   218	    setState(() {
   219	      _busy = true;
   220	      _error = null;
   221	    });
   222	    try {
   223	      for (final item in _items) {
   224	        if (_granted(item.purpose)) {
   225	          await _service.grant(item.purpose, uiSurface: _surface);
   226	        } else {
   227	          await _service.withdraw(item.purpose);
   228	        }
   229	      }
   230	      if (!mounted) return;
   231	      if (widget.onDone != null) {
   232	        widget.onDone!();
   233	      } else {
   234	        Navigator.of(context).pop(true);
   235	      }

 succeeded in 0ms:
     1	# Diagnostic build isolation (#8)
     2	
     3	Problem (issue #8): an in-place install of a clean build over a diagnostic
     4	build inherited the diagnostic native state — iOS BLE state restoration
     5	resumed advertising from persisted token slots and re-activated diagnostic
     6	logging before Dart attached and could revalidate anything.
     7	
     8	Durable fix, by construction rather than by runtime defaults:
     9	
    10	## The `diag` flavor
    11	
    12	Diagnostic builds are a separate Xcode flavor, never the production binary:
    13	
    14	```bash
    15	flutter build ios --flavor diag --release --dart-define=INRANGE_W5_LINKS=true
    16	# artifact: build/ios/iphoneos/Runner.app with bundle id io.inrange.inRange.diag
    17	```
    18	
    19	- **Separate bundle id** `io.inrange.inRange.diag` (build configurations
    20	  `Debug-diag` / `Release-diag` / `Profile-diag`) → separate sandbox
    21	  container, separate keychain/UserDefaults universe. A production install can
    22	  never even see a diag build's persisted state; the two coexist on one phone.
    23	- **`INRANGE_DIAG` compile condition** (set only in the diag configurations,
    24	  see `SWIFT_ACTIVE_COMPILATION_CONDITIONS`): diagnostic-only code paths are
    25	  compiled OUT of production, not defaulted off. Today that covers the native
    26	  wake/soak log (`bb_wake_log.txt` — production binaries contain no writer for
    27	  it). Any future diagnostic instrumentation (e.g. the synthetic-slot injection
    28	  from `diag/w5-token-rotation-repro`) must live under `#if INRANGE_DIAG`.
    29	- **Separate persistence namespaces even if bundle ids were ever collapsed**
    30	  (belt + suspenders): diag builds persist operational state in the
    31	  `io.inrange.diag` UserDefaults suite and register CoreBluetooth restoration
    32	  under `.diag`-suffixed restore identifiers. Production reads
    33	  `UserDefaults.standard` and the unsuffixed restore ids only — there is no
    34	  code path in a production binary that opens the diag suite.
    35	- **Production pre-Dart restoration stays enabled** — `bootFromPersistence()`
    36	  and `willRestoreState` behavior are unchanged for production state.
    37	
    38	## Executable evidence
    39	
    40	`RunnerTests/ReleaseIsolationTests.swift` (runs in the normal, non-diag
    41	configuration):
    42	
    43	- production build reports `isDiagBuild == false`, empty restore-id suffix;
    44	- production restoration identifiers are exactly the unsuffixed ones;
    45	- state written to the diag suite is invisible to the production operational
    46	  domain (`operationalDefaults()` ≡ `UserDefaults.standard`).
    47	
    48	Hardware acceptance still owed (hands-on): install diag build → run a session →
    49	in-place install production build → verify no diag tokens/logging resume
    50	(the original #8 repro, now expected impossible: different container).
    51	
    52	## Plumbing notes
    53	
    54	- Podfile maps the three diag configs (`'Debug-diag' => :debug`, etc.);
    55	  `pod install` generates `Pods-Runner.*-diag.xcconfig`.
    56	- `ios/Flutter/{Debug,Release,Profile}-diag.xcconfig` include the matching
    57	  diag pods xcconfig + `Generated.xcconfig`; the Runner target's diag
    58	  configurations use them as base configurations.
    59	- Scheme `diag` exists so `flutter build ios --flavor diag` resolves.
    60	- The soak/bench workflow changes: instrumented runs (wake log evidence) now

DESCRIPTION
  Deploy a Function to the linked Supabase project.

USAGE
  supabase functions deploy [flags] <Function name...>

  Function name... string  Names of Functions to deploy. Deploys all if omitted.

FLAGS
  --project-ref string    Project ref of the Supabase project.
  --no-verify-jwt         Disable JWT verification for the Function.
  --use-api               Bundle functions server-side without using Docker.
  --import-map string     Path to import map file.
  --prune                 Delete Functions that exist in Supabase project but not locally.
  --jobs, -j integer      Maximum number of parallel jobs.

GLOBAL FLAGS
  --help, -h                                                          Show help information

  --create-ticket                                                     Create a support ticket for any CLI error.

   557	     SET status = CASE WHEN attempts < 5 THEN 'pending' ELSE 'failed' END,
   558	         last_error = 'stale_processing_recovered',
   559	         processing_at = NULL
   560	   WHERE status = 'processing'
   561	     AND processing_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '10 minutes';
   562	
   563	  DELETE FROM public.notification_outbox
   564	   WHERE (status IN ('sent', 'skipped') AND created_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days')
   565	      OR (status = 'failed' AND created_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days');
   566	
   567	  DELETE FROM public.ai_events WHERE created_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '90 days';
   568	  DELETE FROM public.ai_runs   WHERE created_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '90 days';
   569	
   570	  -- Evidence snapshots: 1 year, unless the subject is still held or the
   571	  -- snapshot backs an unexpired (or unfiled) CyberTipline obligation.
   572	  DELETE FROM public.report_evidence e
   573	   WHERE e.captured_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '1 year'
   574	     AND (e.subject_user IS NULL OR NOT public.has_legal_hold(e.subject_user))
   575	     AND NOT EXISTS (
   576	       SELECT 1 FROM public.cybertipline_queue q
   577	        WHERE q.report_id = e.report_id
   578	          AND (q.preserve_until IS NULL OR q.preserve_until > NOW()));
   579	END;
   580	$$;
   581	
   582	COMMENT ON FUNCTION public.cleanup_ephemeral_data IS
   583	  'Sweeps ephemeral tables: location_pings (24 h), sightings (24 h), token_claim_history (24 h), rssi_samples (30 d), venue_anchors (14 d), proximity_wake_requests (30 d sent / 7 d failed), notification_outbox, AI events/runs (90 d), report_evidence (1 y). Honors legal holds.';
   584	
   585	COMMIT;

    25	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    26	-- 1. rssi_samples
    27	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    28	-- Mirrors lib/core/db/local_db.dart:32 (rssi_log), plus the three columns the
    29	-- local table does not need: who, which device, and which local row.
    30	
    31	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.rssi_samples (
    32	  id             BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    33	  user_id        UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    34	  device_id      TEXT NOT NULL,
    35	  platform       TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (platform IN ('ios','android')),
    36	  -- The local rssi_log.id (INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT). Carried so the
    37	  -- natural key below is exact, and so the extractor can detect a GAP in the
    38	  -- sequence — the difference between "the peer went quiet" and "the upload
    39	  -- dropped rows", which RSSI values alone cannot distinguish.
    40	  device_seq     BIGINT NOT NULL,
    41	  -- DEVICE clock, milliseconds. Never server time: extract_walk.py windows on
    42	  -- this and the walk_id digest hashes it, so rewriting it here would break
    43	  -- walk identity. Same client-timestamp pass-through rationale as 0053.
    44	  at_ms          BIGINT NOT NULL,
    45	  correlation_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    46	  rssi           INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (rssi BETWEEN -127 AND 20),
    47	  power          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (power IN ('H','M')),
    48	  received_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
    49	);
    50	
    51	-- Idempotency. Re-uploading a batch must not mint duplicate samples: a walk
    52	-- that ingests twice satisfies the >=3-walk trainer gate with copies of one
    53	-- walk, which is the exact failure the walk_id digest exists to prevent.
    54	--
    55	-- Keyed on device_seq rather than on the sample content. Content is not unique
    56	-- — two adverts can share (at_ms, correlation_id, rssi, power) — so a content
    57	-- key would silently drop real measurements and skew high_n/med_n.
    58	--
    59	-- CLIENT REQUIREMENT: device_seq restarts at 1 if the local DB is recreated, so
    60	-- LocalDb.wipeAll() MUST rotate device_id. Without that, post-wipe rows collide
    61	-- with pre-wipe rows and are dropped by this index.
    62	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uq_rssi_samples_device_seq
    63	  ON public.rssi_samples (user_id, device_id, device_seq);
    64	
    65	-- Extraction: one walk window on one device.
    66	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_rssi_samples_device_time
    67	  ON public.rssi_samples (user_id, device_id, at_ms);
    68	
    69	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_rssi_samples_cleanup
    70	  ON public.rssi_samples (received_at);
    71	
    72	ALTER TABLE public.rssi_samples ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
    73	
    74	-- No INSERT policy: writes go through record_rssi_batch (SECURITY DEFINER) so
    75	-- the batch cap and rate limit cannot be bypassed by a direct table insert.
    76	-- SELECT on own rows only — needed by export_my_data below, and the thing that
    77	-- keeps this table from being a proximity oracle for anyone else.
    78	DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Users read own rssi samples" ON public.rssi_samples;
    79	CREATE POLICY "Users read own rssi samples"
    80	  ON public.rssi_samples FOR SELECT TO authenticated
    81	  USING (user_id = auth.uid());
    82	
    83	REVOKE ALL ON TABLE public.rssi_samples FROM PUBLIC, anon;
    84	GRANT SELECT ON TABLE public.rssi_samples TO authenticated;
    85	GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON TABLE public.rssi_samples TO service_role;
    86	
    87	COMMENT ON TABLE public.rssi_samples IS
    88	  'Raw per-advert RSSI shipped from devices for proximity calibration. Co-location data: rows joined across two users reconstruct who was near whom. Written only while INRANGE_CALIB_SCAN is on; enabling for general users requires a consent record (0039).';
    89	COMMENT ON COLUMN public.rssi_samples.device_seq IS
    90	  'Local rssi_log.id. Natural key for idempotent re-upload and for gap detection. LocalDb.wipeAll() must rotate device_id, since this counter restarts at 1.';
    91	COMMENT ON COLUMN public.rssi_samples.at_ms IS
    92	  'Device clock at sample time, not upload time. extract_walk.py windows on this and the walk_id digest hashes it.';

    89	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.claim_token(p_token text, p_valid_until timestamp with time zone, p_lat double precision DEFAULT NULL::double precision, p_lon double precision DEFAULT NULL::double precision, p_range range_type DEFAULT 'miles_10'::range_type, p_accuracy double precision DEFAULT NULL::double precision)
    90	 RETURNS void
    91	 LANGUAGE plpgsql
    92	 SECURITY DEFINER
    93	 SET search_path TO 'pg_catalog', 'public'
    94	AS $function$
    95	DECLARE
    96	  v_uid UUID := auth.uid();
    97	  v_now TIMESTAMPTZ := clock_timestamp();
    98	  v_last TIMESTAMPTZ;
    99	  v_in_batch BOOLEAN;
   100	BEGIN
   101	  IF v_uid IS NULL THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'Not authenticated' USING ERRCODE='28000'; END IF;
   102	  IF NOT public.current_user_can_discover() THEN
   103	    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Complete age and photo verification before using Beacon' USING ERRCODE='42501'; END IF;
   104	  -- Consent gate (0040). No-op unless app_settings.enforce_consent = 1.
   105	  PERFORM public.require_consent(v_uid, 'ble_proximity');
   106	  -- 0048: the consent UI scopes GPS to precise_location ("deleted after 24h").
   107	  -- Beacon mandatorily uploads coordinates, so a user who withdrew precise
   108	  -- location must not keep feeding GPS through it, even while ble_proximity
   109	  -- is still granted. Explicit withdrawal denies regardless of enforce_consent.
   110	  IF public.consent_withdrawn(v_uid, 'precise_location') THEN
   111	    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Location sharing was turned off' USING ERRCODE='42501'; END IF;
   112	  IF p_token IS NULL OR p_token !~ '^[0-9a-f]{32}$' THEN
   113	    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Invalid beacon token' USING ERRCODE='22023'; END IF;
   114	  IF p_valid_until IS NULL OR p_valid_until <= v_now + INTERVAL '1 minute'
   115	     OR p_valid_until > v_now + INTERVAL '21 minutes' THEN
   116	    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Token validity must end within 1..21 minutes' USING ERRCODE='22023'; END IF;
   117	  IF p_lat IS NULL OR p_lon IS NULL THEN
   118	    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Fresh coordinates are required' USING ERRCODE='22023'; END IF;
   119	  IF p_lat NOT BETWEEN -90 AND 90 OR p_lon NOT BETWEEN -180 AND 180 THEN
   120	    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Invalid coordinates' USING ERRCODE='22023'; END IF;
   121	  IF p_accuracy IS NOT NULL AND (p_accuracy < 0 OR p_accuracy > 10000) THEN

   125	  -- (observability); enforce membership only when the flag is on so the

   132	    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Beacon token was not issued to this account' USING ERRCODE='22023';

   141	
   142	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   143	-- correlate_encounter: gate 3 (+ the same claim grace, + a valid_from floor
   144	-- that can never exclude a late-window-valid claim). Verbatim 0030 body
   145	-- except the three window expressions.
   146	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   147	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.correlate_encounter(
   148	  p_observed_token TEXT, p_lat DOUBLE PRECISION, p_lon DOUBLE PRECISION,
   149	  p_radius_meters DOUBLE PRECISION DEFAULT 50, p_time_window_minutes INT DEFAULT 60
   150	)
   151	RETURNS TABLE (encounter_id BIGINT, other_user_id UUID, created_new BOOLEAN)
   152	LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = pg_catalog, public
   153	AS $$
   154	DECLARE
   155	  v_uid UUID := auth.uid(); v_claim public.token_claim_history%ROWTYPE;
   156	  v_user_a UUID; v_user_b UUID; v_enc_id BIGINT;
   157	  v_distance DOUBLE PRECISION; v_rssi INTEGER; v_min_rssi INTEGER;
   158	  v_new BOOLEAN := FALSE; v_sight_range public.range_type; v_band public.range_type;
   159	  v_reverse_band public.range_type; v_now TIMESTAMPTZ := NOW();
   160	  v_late INTERVAL := public.late_evidence_window();
   161	  v_late_min INT := (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM public.late_evidence_window()) / 60)::INT;
   162	BEGIN
   163	  IF v_uid IS NULL OR NOT public.current_user_can_discover() THEN RETURN; END IF;
   164	  SELECT * INTO v_claim FROM public.token_claim_history tc
   165	  WHERE tc.token = lower(p_observed_token) AND tc.user_id <> v_uid
   166	    -- Floor so a late-window-valid, end-of-life token is never excluded
   167	    -- (token life <=21 min + late window; +2 slack). valid_until is the gate.
   168	    AND tc.valid_from > NOW() - make_interval(mins => GREATEST(23 + v_late_min, LEAST(30, GREATEST(1, p_time_window_minutes))))
   169	    AND tc.valid_until > NOW() - v_late ORDER BY tc.valid_from DESC LIMIT 1;
   170	  IF NOT FOUND OR NOT public.is_discoverable_user(v_claim.user_id) THEN RETURN; END IF;
   171	  IF public.is_blocked_pair(v_uid, v_claim.user_id) THEN RETURN; END IF;
   172	
   173	  SELECT s.rssi, s.range_type INTO v_rssi, v_sight_range FROM public.sightings s
   174	  WHERE s.observer_user_id = v_uid AND s.observed_token = lower(p_observed_token)
   175	  ORDER BY s.observed_at DESC LIMIT 1;
   176	  v_min_rssi := CASE COALESCE(v_claim.range_type,'feet_10') WHEN 'feet_10' THEN -75 WHEN 'feet_20' THEN -85 ELSE -95 END;
   177	  IF v_rssi IS NULL OR v_rssi < v_min_rssi THEN RETURN; END IF;
   178	
   179	  IF p_lat IS NOT NULL AND p_lon IS NOT NULL AND v_claim.approx_lat IS NOT NULL AND v_claim.approx_lon IS NOT NULL THEN
   180	    v_distance := ST_Distance(ST_SetSRID(ST_MakePoint(p_lon, p_lat),4326)::geography, ST_SetSRID(ST_MakePoint(v_claim.approx_lon, v_claim.approx_lat),4326)::geography);
   181	    IF v_distance > LEAST(400.0, GREATEST(5.0, p_radius_meters)) THEN RETURN; END IF;
   182	  END IF;
   183	
   184	  IF v_sight_range IS NOT NULL AND v_sight_range::TEXT LIKE 'feet_%' THEN v_band := v_sight_range; ELSE v_band := COALESCE(v_claim.range_type, 'feet_10'); END IF;
   185	
   186	  -- Reciprocity gate (server-receipt window; caller-supplied values ignored).
   187	  -- 0053: widened from a fixed 3 min — the other side's evidence may be a
   188	  -- locked phone's wake-burst upload from earlier in the same co-presence.
   189	  SELECT rs.range_type INTO v_reverse_band FROM public.sightings rs
   190	  WHERE rs.observer_user_id = v_claim.user_id AND rs.observed_user_id = v_uid
   191	    AND rs.received_at > NOW() - v_late
   192	  ORDER BY rs.received_at DESC LIMIT 1;
   193	  IF NOT FOUND THEN RETURN; END IF;
   194	
   195	  IF v_reverse_band IS NOT NULL AND v_reverse_band::TEXT LIKE 'feet_%' AND v_band::TEXT LIKE 'feet_%'
   196	     AND public.range_band_rank(v_reverse_band) > public.range_band_rank(v_band) THEN
   197	    v_band := v_reverse_band;
   198	  END IF;
   199	
   200	  v_user_a := LEAST(v_uid, v_claim.user_id); v_user_b := GREATEST(v_uid, v_claim.user_id);
   201	  PERFORM pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended(v_user_a::TEXT || v_user_b::TEXT, 0));
   202	  PERFORM public.bump_encounter_pair(v_user_a, v_user_b, v_band);
   203	  UPDATE public.encounter_pairs SET trust_level = COALESCE(trust_level, 'mutual_ble')

    89	  IF p_lat NOT BETWEEN -90 AND 90 OR p_lon NOT BETWEEN -180 AND 180 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'Invalid coordinates' USING ERRCODE='22023'; END IF;
    90	  IF p_accuracy IS NOT NULL AND (p_accuracy < 0 OR p_accuracy > 10000) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'Invalid accuracy' USING ERRCODE='22023'; END IF;

docs/research/2026-07-31/claude_kimi_chat_2026-07-31.md-302-Correctness: probe 4 is the concrete proof hazypiff asked for. Without in-handshake alias continuity, keeper-down-during-rotation is a demonstrated silent-lease-replacement + unbounded liveness wedge; with the alias known (my control test) the same flow re-commits cleanly. ALIAS_ROLL-over-keeper alone cannot cover the case because the channel it rides is exactly what's down.
docs/research/2026-07-31/claude_kimi_chat_2026-07-31.md-303-
docs/research/2026-07-31/claude_kimi_chat_2026-07-31.md-304-Privacy: prevAlias reaches back exactly one generation and is exposed only inside HELLO — i.e., to an already-connected peer over the GATT link, not in the broadcast advert. A connected peer learns alias continuity anyway whenever ALIAS_ROLL succeeds, so the marginal exposure is limited to the roll-lost case and bounded to one 15-min generation. That is a small price against a proven correctness hole. Hardening to bake in: send all-zero once the peer has acknowledged the new alias (or at `prevAliasExpiry`), so linkage doesn't persist beyond the recovery window; never carry more than one generation back.

docs/research/2026-07-31/claude_kimi_chat_2026-07-31.md-302-Correctness: probe 4 is the concrete proof hazypiff asked for. Without in-handshake alias continuity, keeper-down-during-rotation is a demonstrated silent-lease-replacement + unbounded liveness wedge; with the alias known (my control test) the same flow re-commits cleanly. ALIAS_ROLL-over-keeper alone cannot cover the case because the channel it rides is exactly what's down.
docs/research/2026-07-31/claude_kimi_chat_2026-07-31.md-303-
docs/research/2026-07-31/claude_kimi_chat_2026-07-31.md-304-Privacy: prevAlias reaches back exactly one generation and is exposed only inside HELLO — i.e., to an already-connected peer over the GATT link, not in the broadcast advert. A connected peer learns alias continuity anyway whenever ALIAS_ROLL succeeds, so the marginal exposure is limited to the roll-lost case and bounded to one 15-min generation. That is a small price against a proven correctness hole. Hardening to bake in: send all-zero once the peer has acknowledged the new alias (or at `prevAliasExpiry`), so linkage doesn't persist beyond the recovery window; never carry more than one generation back.

     1	# Spec — cloud upload for calibration RSSI samples
     2	
     3	Step 1 (server) is **implemented and tested**: `supabase/migrations/0056_calibration_rssi_samples.sql`,
     4	`supabase/tests/rssi_samples_test.sql`. Steps 2–4 (client, extractor) are **spec only**.
     5	
     6	Written 2026-07-24.
     7	
     8	## Why
     9	
    10	Today an iPhone's calibration data is trapped behind `xcrun devicectl` on Rahul's Mac.
    11	`rssi_log` is local SQLite; the only way off the phone is a USB pull by a person who
    12	has the phone. That does not scale past two testers, and it does not work at all for
    13	real users — you cannot USB-pull a stranger's phone.
    14	
    15	This ships `rssi_log` rows to Supabase so a walk can be extracted without the device
    16	in hand.
    17	
    18	## The one thing to get right first
    19	
    20	`rssi_samples` is a **raw co-location log**: each row says "this user was within BLE
    21	range of this correlation ID at this instant, at this signal strength." Two of those
    22	streams joined server-side reconstruct exactly who was near whom, when — which is the
    23	thing the encounter pipeline deliberately withholds behind the 4-hour reveal delay
    24	(`ENCOUNTER_REVEAL_DELAY_HOURS`) and the consent gates in `0040_wire_consent_gates.sql`.
    25	
    26	For a lab walk with two consenting testers under `INRANGE_CALIB_SCAN=true`, that is
    27	fine and it is the point. **Turning this on for real users is not a config change** —
    28	it is a new data category that needs a consent record (`0039_consent_records.sql`), a
    29	retention decision, and a line in the privacy policy. Uploads stay gated client-side
    30	on `AppConfig.calibScanMode` precisely so that decision stays explicit.
    31	
    32	## Server — done
    33	
    34	`0056_calibration_rssi_samples.sql` adds `public.rssi_samples` + `public.rssi_batch_rate`
    35	and the `record_rssi_batch(p_device_id, p_platform, p_samples jsonb)` RPC (house style is
    36	RPC-over-table-insert — 25 `.rpc()` call sites vs 1 `.from().insert()`). Writes go only
    37	through the RPC: `authenticated` has `SELECT` on own rows and no `INSERT`, so the batch
    38	cap and rate limit cannot be bypassed.
    39	
    40	Four decisions worth knowing before writing the client:
    41	
    42	**Idempotency is keyed on `device_seq`, not on sample content.** `device_seq` is the
    43	local `rssi_log.id`. A content key — `(at_ms, correlation_id, rssi, power)` — looks
    44	natural and is wrong: two adverts can legitimately share all four, so a content key
    45	silently drops real measurements and skews `high_n`/`med_n` in the trained features.
    46	Keying on the local rowid also gives **gap detection** for free, which is the only way
    47	to tell "the peer went quiet" from "the upload dropped rows."

   104	  SELECT rn, t INTO v_pos, v_total
   105	  FROM (
   106	    SELECT id,
   107	           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY priority DESC, id ASC) AS rn,
   108	           COUNT(*) OVER () AS t
   109	    FROM public.waitlist
   110	  ) x
   111	  WHERE x.id = v_row.id;
   112	
   113	  IF v_row.zone IS NOT NULL THEN
   114	    SELECT COUNT(*) INTO v_zone_count FROM public.waitlist WHERE zone = v_row.zone;
   115	    SELECT rnk INTO v_zone_rank FROM (
   116	      SELECT zone, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rnk
   117	      FROM public.waitlist WHERE zone IS NOT NULL GROUP BY zone
   118	    ) z WHERE z.zone = v_row.zone;
   119	  END IF;
   120	
   121	  RETURN jsonb_build_object(
   122	    'position',       v_pos,
   123	    'total',          v_total,
   124	    'behind',         v_total - v_pos,
   125	    'ref_code',       v_row.ref_code,
   126	    'referral_count', (SELECT referral_count FROM public.waitlist WHERE id = v_row.id),
   127	    'new',            v_new,
   128	    'zone',           v_row.zone,
   129	    'zone_count',     v_zone_count,
   130	    'zone_rank',      v_zone_rank
   131	  );
   132	END;
   133	$$;
   134	
   135	REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.join_waitlist(TEXT, TEXT, TEXT, TEXT) FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated;
   136	GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.join_waitlist(TEXT, TEXT, TEXT, TEXT) TO service_role;
   137	
   138	COMMIT;

# In Range — full-system hardening & bug-hunt audit, 2026-08-01

**Scope:** stability, security, correctness. No UI/UX work.
**Branches reviewed:** `main` @ `f2f948e`, `fix/w5-encounter-lease` @ `83890e6` (PR #9),
`feat/gamification-phase-a` (PR #10).
**Panel:** 7 independent Claude reviewers + Kimi CLI + Codex CLI (`gpt-5.6-sol`, max reasoning),
each on a separate scope, plus a live production probe.

**Verification rule applied to every finding below:** nothing entered this report on a reviewer's
say-so. Each finding was re-checked against the code by the coordinating agent, and the specific
evidence is recorded in `verified_findings_working.md`. Reviewer claims that did not survive
verification were corrected or dropped, and the corrections are noted inline. Two corrections were
material enough to change how a finding should be read (C-DIAG-1 and H-DIAG-3).

**Baseline established:** `flutter analyze` clean; `flutter test` 183/183 on main, 233/233 on the W5
branch. Both suites are green — none of the defects below is caught by an existing test.

---

## VERDICT

**Not ready to trust in the wild.** Ten Critical findings, of which **one is live in production and
remotely exploitable by anyone on the internet right now**, and five more are exploitable today by any
authenticated user with a modified client.

The single most important structural observation: **the three worst classes of defect here are all
"invariant enforced by hand-applied convention, with nothing proving coverage."** Consent checks,
retention purges, and service-role auth are each applied per-call-site by a human remembering to do it.
Every miss in this report is a miss of that kind. Two tests (below, §Systemic) would have caught five
Criticals at authoring time.

---

## CRITICAL

### C-PROD-1 🔴 LIVE — `photo-review` and `send-push` accept unauthenticated requests in production
**Deploy drift, not a source defect. The repo code is correct.**
Probed directly: `POST /photo-review` with no auth → `200`; with a *wrong* bearer → `200`;
**`GET` with no auth → `200`**. `requireServiceRole` rejects non-POST with 405 before anything else, so a
200 on GET proves the deployed binary lacks the check entirely. `POST /send-push` no auth → `200`,
`{"processed":19}`. Control: `maintenance` correctly returns `401`.

The gate landed in `45ef624` (2026-07-12) for all four functions; only `maintenance` (v5) and
`miles-correlate` (v6) were redeployed — `SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md:31-32` names exactly those two.
**~3 weeks of production running pre-hardening code.**

`photo-review` reports `auto_approve: true` on the production host, and photo verification is the control
gating discoverability (0052) — a moderation step adjacent to child-safety obligations. `send-push` drains
the outbox and leaks internal row ids; it is harmless only because FCM credentials are unset.

**Fix now:** `supabase functions deploy send-push photo-review`; set `verify_jwt=false` for both (currently
`true`, which rejects the `sb_secret_` service key — the legitimate caller is the only one locked out); add
the missing `[functions.proximity-wake]` block (it currently 404s).

### C-SQL-1 🔴 `claim_token` overwrites another user's `token_claim_history` row
`0060:149-159` — `ON CONFLICT (token) DO UPDATE` with **no `WHERE user_id = v_uid`**. The `COALESCE`
"guard" is dead code: `0060:117-118` rejects NULL coordinates, so `EXCLUDED.approx_lat` is always non-NULL
and always wins. Tokens are broadcast in plaintext over BLE, so any modified client harvests them.
**Neutralises the GPS veto** — `correlate_encounter` (`0053:179-182`) compares against coordinates the
attacker just wrote. Mitigating check is behind `enforce_batch_tokens`, which is **0**.
**Fix:** add `WHERE public.token_claim_history.user_id = v_uid` to the `DO UPDATE`.

### C-SQL-2 🔴 `correlate_miles_encounters` fabricates encounters from arbitrary GPS
`0048:251-360`, reached via `record_location_ping` (`0019:1227`), granted to `authenticated`
(`0008:263`, never revoked — 0061's sweep is `anon`-only by design). Inserts into `public.encounters` for
up to 100 peers per call with **no `trust_level` and no reciprocity check**. There are two encounter
producers and only the BLE one was hardened by 0029→0053. Also returns raw `user_id`s of real users near
an attacker-chosen point — a presence/identity oracle.
**Fix:** stop this path writing `encounters` (own table), or stamp `trust_level='gps_only'` and exclude it
everywhere encounters are treated as evidence; stop returning `other_user_id` to `authenticated`.

### C-SQL-3 🔴 `beacon_token_batch` has no scheduled purge — a permanent token→user_id map
`cleanup_ephemeral_data()` (latest: `0059:477-580`) purges 9 tables; this is not one of them. Every
`DELETE` of it is either self-scoped inside `issue_token_batch` or an account-deletion path.
`JOIN beacon_token_batch b ON b.token = rssi_samples.correlation_id` yields a fully de-anonymised
30-day proximity graph. Users who churn leave their token set on the server permanently.
**Fix (2 lines):** `DELETE FROM public.beacon_token_batch WHERE valid_until < NOW() - INTERVAL '24 hours';`
The `idx_beacon_token_batch_expiry` index already exists for it.

### C-SQL-4 🔴 Batch-pre-claimed tokens skip the GPS veto entirely *(found by Kimi K3, verified)*
`0053:179-182` wraps the spatial veto in `IF ... v_claim.approx_lat IS NOT NULL ...`. `claim_token`
requires coordinates, but `claim_token_batch` (`0060:25`) pre-claims the whole batch with NULL location —
the locked-phone path 0060 exists to serve. For any token claimed that way the veto **does not run at
all**. Independent of C-SQL-1: fixing the cross-user overwrite does not close this.
**Fix:** treat a location-less claim as veto-*failing*, or fall back to comparing the two sightings'
`observer_lat/lon` to each other (always present).

### C-CONSENT-1 🔴 The three newest telemetry write paths have no consent check at all
`require_consent`/`consent_withdrawn` appear **zero times** in `0056` and `0059`. `record_rssi_batch`
checks auth, device-id, JSON type and a row cap — no purpose. `enqueue_proximity_wake` checks auth and a
throttle — no purpose. `venue_anchors` has no RPC at all; the client writes the table directly under RLS.
Worse than the earlier audit's defect, which checked the *wrong* purpose; these check *none*.

### C-DIAG-1 🔴 Diagnostic W5 link layer ships in release binaries
The entire iOS tree has **three** `#if INRANGE_DIAG` sites, all in `BackgroundBeacon.swift`.
`W5LinkController.swift` (701 lines) has zero. Its gate is the persisted bool `bb.w5links` (`:120`), and
`recordRssi` (`:633-650`) appends plaintext `{"token":"<hex>","rssi":N,"ts":…}` to
`Documents/w5_rssi_log.jsonl`.
**Correction applied:** the reviewer said this write is ungated; verification shows the effective gate is
`bb.w5links` (sessions only form behind it at `:956`). The finding stands and is *cleaner* stated
correctly — issue #8's whole point is that a persisted flag must not be what stands between a release
binary and diagnostic behaviour, because the stale value is `true` until Dart overwrites it.

### C-W5-1 🔴 A committed encounter reached by `realId` bypasses the sticky-keeper branch
Verified in both languages: the committed check precedes the `realId` fallback —
Dart `w5_ownership.dart:321` vs `:351`; Swift `W5Ownership.swift:250` vs `:279`. A reviewer *executed*
the Dart case: keeper silently moves `p1→p2`, no close of the intruder, no `owns` emitted.
Violates the design doc's "committed keeper is sticky" rule (`:295-296`).
**Trigger needs no attacker:** `HELLO_ACK` has no `prevAlias` field, so on the outbound path a rotated
peer alias is unresolvable by construction. Reopens the #7 duplicate-keeper defect.
**Fix:** hoist the `realId` resolution above the committed check in both implementations.

### C-W5-2 🔴 Peripheral restoration permanently nils the notify characteristics
`BackgroundBeacon.swift:736-751` restores the service and sets `serviceAdded = true` but never re-binds
`controlNotifyChar`/`keepaliveNotifyChar`, which are created only inside `if !serviceAdded`. After a
restoration relaunch the peripheral can never send HELLO_ACK, PROPOSE, ACK, REJECT, or a keepalive notify
— while still advertising and answering reads, so it looks healthy. For an app designed around iOS
relaunching it for BLE events, this is the **normal** path.

### C-RT-1 🔴 `_flushSightings` has no re-entrancy guard; "turn beacon off" can hang ~83 minutes
`beacon_service.dart:417-422`. The 45s timer fires an unawaited, unguarded flush that awaits up to 500
RPCs sequentially at a 10s timeout. On the half-dead-network condition this file itself documents, one
pass takes ~83 min and the timer starts 111 more. Every sibling drain in the codebase is guarded; this
one's omission looks accidental. `turnOffBeacon` awaits it while holding `_busy`, so the user taps off and
BLE keeps running for up to 83 minutes.

---

## HIGH (summary — detail in `verified_findings_working.md`)

- **H-CFG-1** `verify_jwt` is set inversely to risk. `send-push` and `photo-review` are `true` (rejects the
  `sb_secret_` key); `proximity-wake` has **no config entry at all**. Compounds C-PROD-1.
- **H-WL-1** `join_waitlist` performs an **unauthenticated cross-user UPDATE** and returns another
  person's `ref_code`, zone and position (`0062:100-104`, `:120-131`) — live on prod, no JWT, CORS `*`.
- **H-WL-2** Waitlist **email-enumeration oracle**: `0054:74-76` shipped `RETURNS VOID` with the comment
  "the caller can't tell whether an address was already on the list (no enumeration oracle)". 0055/0062
  replaced it with a JSONB ladder carrying `new` — **the stated property was silently dropped and its
  comment left behind asserting it still holds.**
- **H-DIAG-2** `ReleaseIsolationTests` cannot fail — asserts compile-time constants, CI runs Debug only
  (`ios-build.yml:52`). Adding `INRANGE_DIAG` to Release would keep CI green.
- **H-DIAG-3** Pre-Dart restoration trusts persisted state incl. a bearer token POSTed by `sendWakePing`.
  **Correction applied:** the reviewer called this an unimplemented requirement; the source comments show
  pre-Dart boot is *deliberate* (the point of the W2 wiring). The fix must be a persisted flavor/schema
  stamp that wipes foreign state — not "wait for Dart".
- **H-ORCH-1** Round-8 sign-off evidence is partly unreproducible: ~20 of the 26 cited adversarial probes
  were never committed and their source directory is gone. The bug class they pin can regress silently.
- **H-W5-3** No lease persistence exists, and restoration actively re-handshakes restored links with
  *fresh* identity, which the peer correctly rejects — costing a ≥5-min blackout plus a wedged lease.
- **H-W5-4** `dropPeer` (user pressed pass) never erases the lease and does not disconnect an inbound
  keeper at all; `onTeardown` has **no production caller**. The app can re-dial someone the user rejected.
- **H-W5-5** The per-encounter candidate is keyed by peer alias, so token rotation mints a new candidate —
  R7 fix #1 is dead code in production and rotation-during-grace forks a duplicate encounter.
- **H-RT-2** RH-1 is unfixed on all three counts, and the foreground-service heartbeat runs in a *separate
  engine*, so the notification clock keeps ticking over a dead scanner — the one signal a field tester
  could have used is a false positive by construction.
- **H-RT-3** Natively-buffered sightings are replayed into the live 90s window with fresh timestamps →
  false "Close By" for a peer who was near 20 minutes ago, and it hides a dead scanner from the watchdog.
- **H-RT-4** `turnOffBeacon` is the only lifecycle path with no session-generation guard (6 awaits).
- **H-RT-5** An unvalidated server token crashes the beacon: `_hexTo16Bytes` throws on anything not
  32 hex chars, and `_rotateToken`'s catch then **silently disables the beacon**.
- **H-RT-6** The consent gate is a one-shot prefs flag — withdrawal never re-gates; `preciseLocation`
  withdrawal does not stop the beacon's GPS; WiFi scanning is bound to no purpose at all.
- **H-RT-7** `myEncountersProvider` is not user-scoped and is absent from `_clearUserRuntime` — **user A's
  server encounters render for user B** after an account switch. Same class as the consent-provider bug
  that was fixed; the fix was never swept across the other providers.
- **H-RT-8** Backgrounded-iPhone discovery is broken by Apple multi-AD blob offsets on Android 15/16. The
  remedy is fully implemented in `apple_overflow_bit.dart` + `AdvertParser.kt` and **is not called from
  Dart** — ~1,000 lines of correct machinery dead while the broken constant ships.
- **H-RT-9** `LocalDb.open()` is unguarded in `main()` before `runApp`, and there is no `onDowngrade` —
  a corrupt, full, or downgraded DB bricks launch with no recovery path.
- **H-SQL-4** `scan_relay_abuse` flags the **victim** (`0033:168`), so an attacker can plant abuse flags on
  any user. Becomes Critical the day the mint ships, because blueprint X1 consumes those flags — handing
  an attacker silent, targeted, unappealable suppression of a chosen user's income.
- **H-PW-1** `enqueue_proximity_wake` accepts any geohash with no proof the caller is there, and
  `findLikelyPeers` performs **no blocks / discoverability / consent check** (contrast miles-correlate,
  which does all three). Not live (0059 undeployed + function 404s).
- **H-PRIV-1** Native wake buffer persists up to 50 raw GPS fixes in `UserDefaults` with a **count** cap
  and no age limit, and no path ever clears it — survives updates, included in backups.
- **H-PRIV-2** Release-reachable PII in logs (full correlation id, user UUID, peer MAC, venue geohash).
  The "PII log gating" a prior audit called for **was never built** — no `piiSafe` helper exists, and
  `debugPrint` is not stripped in release.

## MEDIUM / LOW

23 further findings recorded in the working file, including: unsalted SHA-256 of client IP used as a
primary key (reversible in seconds — defeats the "raw IPs are never stored" claim); `venue_anchors`
geohash precision is a comment not a constraint, with 14/30-day retention against a 24h promise;
`bb_wake_log.txt` has no cap or rotation and `FileHandle.write` **traps** on a full disk; Dart↔Swift effect
*ordering* diverges (insertion order vs sorted) and no vector pins it; the Dart codec test cannot detect a
decoder field permutation that the Swift test would catch; `_pendingByCorr` FIFO eviction lets one hostile
advertiser silently blind every user in a room.

---

## WHAT THE VECTORS DO NOT PIN

The conformance vectors are billed as the only thing holding the two W5 implementations together. There
are **4** of them, and the shared runners cannot even express six oracle entry points (`onBeaconOff`,
`onDialFailed`, `onAliasRoll`, `onPrevAliasExpiry`, `onRetryTimer`, `debugSetViewGen`). `sendPropose` and
`sendAck` are matched as **wildcards**, so v5.2 correction #5 (route identity) has zero coverage.
**Note:** the brief for this round referred to "vectors 5+6 pinning the per-alias candidate mint" —
those vectors **do not exist**; the file contains 4. Whoever recorded the R8-F1 follow-up as landed
should re-check it.

## SYSTEMIC — the two tests that would have caught five Criticals

1. A pgTAP assertion that **every RPC inserting into a user-scoped table calls `require_consent`**
   → catches C-CONSENT-1.
2. A retention test that **fails when a table is added to the schema without an entry in
   `cleanup_ephemeral_data`** → catches C-SQL-3 and the `venue_anchors`/`proximity_wake_requests` overruns.
3. A deploy-parity check that probes each Edge Function for `405` on `GET` → catches C-PROD-1 and would
   have caught it three weeks ago.

## RECOMMENDED FIX ORDER

1. **C-PROD-1** — redeploy `send-push` + `photo-review`, fix `verify_jwt`, add the `proximity-wake` entry.
2. **C-SQL-1, C-SQL-2, C-SQL-3, C-CONSENT-1** — four SQL fixes, all small, all live today.
3. **H-WL-1 / H-WL-2** — the only endpoints an anonymous attacker can reach, both live.
4. **C-W5-1** — two-line hoist in each implementation + the vector that pins it.
5. **C-W5-2, C-W5-3, C-RT-1** — the three wedges.
6. **C-DIAG-1 / H-DIAG-2** — compile-out and a guard that can actually fail.
7. Systemic tests above, then the High list.

## COVERAGE AND LIMITATIONS — stated plainly

- **Verified against production:** only the Edge Function auth probe. Everything else is verified against
  source and migrations. Prior lessons in this project ("verify prod, don't infer from migration files")
  apply: the highest-value manual check is `SELECT jobname, schedule FROM cron.job;` — if the
  `in-range-maintenance` row is missing, every retention claim in this report is "forever" instead of 24h.
  `0015`'s `cron.schedule` is wrapped in a `DO $$ ... EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN NULL` block, so a failed
  schedule is **silent**.
- **Not verified:** anything requiring Xcode (no Mac here) — all Swift findings are static reads;
  hardware behaviour; the deployed Edge Function *source* (inferred from response shape + probe).
- **Local Supabase container is at 0019**, so grant checks against it are only authoritative pre-0020.
# Hardening round 2026-08-01 — verified findings (working file)

Findings below are verified by me directly against code/repo state, not taken on a
reviewer's word. Each carries the evidence command or file:line that proves it.

---

## H-ORCH-1 — Round-8 sign-off evidence is partially unreproducible; ~20 adversarial probes lost

**Severity:** High (process / regression-coverage, not a runtime defect)
**Branch:** `fix/w5-encounter-lease` @ `83890e6`

**Claim on record (PR #9, round-8 PASS comment + project memory):** executable evidence
for the software green-light was "Kimi ported round-7 suite 16/16 (probe-4 gone) + 10 new
adversarial probes; Claude re-ran 26/26; Dart 259/259". The regression file was recorded as
`/tmp/kimi-r7/test/features/beacon/w5_ownership_r7_kimi_test.dart` and explicitly noted as
"uncommitted, machine-local".

**Verified state today (2026-08-01):**

| Fact | Evidence |
|---|---|
| W5 branch Dart suite = **233/233**, not 259 | `flutter test` on worktree of `fix/w5-encounter-lease` |
| main Dart suite = **183/183** | `flutter test` on `/home/hazypiff/in-range` |
| Kimi r7 suite file **does not exist** | `ls /tmp/kimi-r7/...` → missing (tmp cleared) |
| It was **never committed on any branch** | `git log --all --oneline --name-only \| grep -i 'r7_kimi\|w5_ownership_r7'` → no match |
| Only **6** probes are committed | `test/features/beacon/zz_probe_test.dart` = 6 `test(` cases |

233 (committed) + 26 (machine-local) = 259 — which reconciles the sign-off number exactly and
confirms the 26 probes were counted as evidence but never landed in the repo.

**Why this matters.** The round-7 defect (probe-4 alias-stomp wedge: lost ALIAS_ROLL +
keeper-down grace → `onDiscovered` stomps an in-grace `_Enc`, generation reset, permanent
stale-gen wedge) was the single most severe correctness bug found in this subsystem. The tests
that pin it are, for the most part, gone: ~20 of the 26 probes cited in the PASS are not in the
repo, not in CI, and their source directory has been deleted. The bug class can regress silently
and the next reviewer will see a green suite.

This also means the round-8 PASS cannot be independently re-verified as written — an auditor
today can reproduce 233 of the 259 claimed assertions.

**Fix:** reconstruct the lost probes as committed tests under
`test/features/beacon/` (they must run in CI), and adopt a standing rule that no review round
may cite an uncommitted test file as sign-off evidence. Any probe that justifies a PASS must be
committed in the same change that claims it.

**Confidence:** CERTAIN (reproduced every fact above on this machine).

---

## C-DIAG-1 — Diagnostic W5 link layer + plaintext RSSI log ship in production binaries, gated only by a persisted bool

**Severity:** Critical (privacy: plaintext proximity records written by a release build)
**Branch:** `fix/w5-encounter-lease`

**Verified evidence:**
- The ENTIRE iOS tree contains exactly **three** `#if INRANGE_DIAG` sites, all in
  `BackgroundBeacon.swift` (lines 52, 68, 694). `W5LinkController.swift` (701 lines,
  the second diagnostic subsystem) has **zero**.
  Proof: `grep -rn INRANGE_DIAG ios/Runner/ ios/RunnerTests/`
- The W5 activation gate is a persisted runtime boolean, not a compile-time flag:
  `BackgroundBeacon.swift:120` → `var w5LinksEnabled: Bool { defaults.bool(forKey: Self.keyW5Links) }`,
  key `"bb.w5links"` (`:124`), written only from the Dart method channel (`:294`).
- `W5LinkController.recordRssi()` (`:633-650`) appends
  `{"token":"<hex>","rssi":N,"ts":<epoch ms>}` to `Documents/w5_rssi_log.jsonl`
  whenever the app is not foreground-active. No compile-time gate.
- Call site `BackgroundBeacon.swift:1227` (`didReadRSSI`) invokes it for any peer in the
  W5 session map.

**CORRECTION to the reviewer's framing (verified):** the reviewer wrote that `recordRssi`
"has no gate at all". That overstates it. W5 sessions only enter the `w5[]` map behind
`if w5LinksEnabled` (`BackgroundBeacon.swift:956`), so the effective gate on the file write
IS `bb.w5links`. The finding survives the correction and is arguably worse framed correctly:
issue #8's stated requirement is that a persisted flag must NOT be the thing standing between
a release binary and diagnostic behavior, because the stale persisted value is `true` until
Dart overwrites it. That is exactly this mechanism.

**Impact:** a release build that inherits `bb.w5links=true` from a prior diag install forms
W5 links and writes plaintext BLE token hex + RSSI + timestamps to `Documents/` before Dart
attaches. Token hex + timestamp is proximity-linkable data in a build whose privacy posture
says it is not collected.

**Fix:** `#if INRANGE_DIAG`-wrap `w5LinksEnabled` (`#else false`), wrap the `recordRssi` file
branch, and exclude `W5LinkController.swift` from the production target's Sources phase until
W5 actually ships.

**Confidence:** CERTAIN (every line above read directly).

---

## H-DIAG-2 — `ReleaseIsolationTests` cannot fail; the #8 guard is not a guard

**Severity:** High (false assurance)

**Verified evidence:**
- `ios/RunnerTests/ReleaseIsolationTests.swift:11-14` asserts
  `XCTAssertFalse(BackgroundBeacon.isDiagBuild)` and `restoreIDSuffix == ""`. Both are
  **compile-time constants** selected by `#if INRANGE_DIAG`.
- CI runs the suite only under Debug: `.github/workflows/ios-build.yml:52` →
  `-configuration Debug`; `Runner.xcscheme:44` TestAction `buildConfiguration = "Debug"`.
- Debug never defines `INRANGE_DIAG` (confirmed: only 3 occurrences in `project.pbxproj`,
  all on the Runner target's three `-diag` configurations).
- Therefore in the only configuration ever tested, the asserted values are true by
  construction. **If someone added `INRANGE_DIAG` to the Release configuration, CI would
  stay green.**
- `testProductionDomainCannotSeeDiagnosticState` (`:24-43`) asserts that
  `UserDefaults.standard` cannot read keys written to a named suite — a restatement of
  Foundation semantics, true in any codebase.
- `diag.xcscheme` has an empty `<Testables>` element: no test ever runs against a diag
  configuration, so there is no positive control proving the `.diag` suffix works either.

**Fix:** assert the property at build-configuration level, not runtime — a CI step running
`xcodebuild -showBuildSettings -configuration Release` and failing if `INRANGE_DIAG` appears,
for each production config; plus a mirrored diag-side test with a populated `<Testables>`.

**Confidence:** CERTAIN.

---

## H-DIAG-3 — Pre-Dart restoration trusts persisted operational state (issue #8 leg (c) unimplemented)

**Severity:** High

**Verified evidence:** `BackgroundBeacon.swift:184` →
`if defaults.bool(forKey: Self.keyEnabled) { ensureManagers(); scheduleWake() }`,
invoked unconditionally from `AppDelegate.swift:17` before the Flutter engine exists.
`sendWakePing()` (`:670-686`) reads a persisted endpoint URL **and a persisted bearer token**
and POSTs to them from a BGTask, with no compile-time gate and no Dart revalidation.

**IMPORTANT CONTEXT the reviewer omitted (verified in code comments):** this is *deliberate*.
`AppDelegate.swift:12-16` states the design intent — "if iOS relaunched us for a bluetooth
event … the persisted flag brings CoreBluetooth back up immediately, before (and without)
the Flutter engine." Pre-Dart boot is the entire point of the W2 background-BLE wiring. So
this is a design tension, not an oversight, and the fix must NOT be "wait for Dart".

**Fix that preserves the design:** persist a flavor/schema stamp (`bb.stateSchema`) next to
the operational state and, on boot, wipe `bb.*` and skip `ensureManagers()` when the stamp is
missing or foreign. That keeps pre-Dart BLE resurrection for genuine same-flavor state while
refusing state written by a different build. Separately, `#if`-gate `sendWakePing` and refuse
token slots whose validity window extends beyond a sane horizon.

**Confidence:** CERTAIN (mechanism); the design-intent framing is quoted from source comments.

## 🔴 C-PROD-1 — LIVE: `photo-review` and `send-push` accept UNAUTHENTICATED requests in production

**Severity:** CRITICAL — remotely exploitable by anyone on the internet, right now.
**This is a DEPLOY-DRIFT defect, not a source defect. The repo code is correct.**

**Verified by direct probe of production (`riigipzlyqeaadyvbuty.supabase.co`), 2026-08-01:**

| Function | Request | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `maintenance` | POST, no auth | `401 {"ok":false,"error":"unauthorized"}` ✅ correct |
| `send-push` | POST, no auth | **`200 {"ok":true,"dry_run":true,"processed":19,...}`** ❌ |
| `photo-review` | POST, no auth | **`200 {"ok":true,"auto_approve":true,"processed":0}`** ❌ |
| `photo-review` | POST, **wrong** bearer | **`200`** ❌ |
| `photo-review` | **GET**, no auth | **`200`** ❌ |
| `proximity-wake` | POST | `404` — not deployed |

The GET result is conclusive. `requireServiceRole` (`supabase/functions/_shared/service_auth.ts:7-9`) rejects any
non-POST with `405 method_not_allowed` **before** anything else. A `200` on GET proves the deployed
binary does not contain that check at all.

**Root cause — deploy drift.** `requireServiceRole` was added to all four functions in commit
`45ef624` (2026-07-12, "fix: harden beta security and reliability"). Only `maintenance` (v5) and
`miles-correlate` (v6) were ever redeployed — see `docs/SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md:31-32`, which names exactly
those two. `send-push` and `photo-review` have been running **pre-2026-07-12 code in production for
~3 weeks**, with no auth gate.

**Impact:**
1. `photo-review` reports `auto_approve: true` **on the production host**. In current source, auto-approve
   requires `isLocal` (`photo-review/index.ts:108-110`), so the deployed build's gating differs. Photo
   verification is the control that gates discoverability (0052) and is a child-safety / NCII-adjacent
   moderation step. An anonymous caller can drive that queue.
2. `send-push` drains `notification_outbox` and returns internal row ids and statuses to an anonymous
   caller. It is currently `dry_run` only because FCM credentials are unset — the moment they are
   configured, an anonymous caller can trigger real push delivery to users.
3. Both leak operational internals (row counts, ids, per-row reasons) to unauthenticated callers.

**Immediate remediation (do this before any other fix in this round):**
`supabase functions deploy send-push photo-review` (and set `verify_jwt=false` for both, plus add a
missing `[functions.proximity-wake]` block, so the `sb_secret_` service key is accepted — see H-CFG-1).
Until redeployed, consider disabling both functions in the dashboard.

**Confidence:** CERTAIN — probed production directly, three independent request shapes.

**⚠️ SIDE EFFECT I CAUSED, DISCLOSED:** my first probe was an unauthenticated POST to `send-push`.
The deployed function processed 19 `notification_outbox` rows and marked them
`status='skipped', last_error='no_device_token'` — a terminal state (`send-push/index.ts:315-324`).
Those 19 rows had no registered device token, so they were undeliverable regardless and no user lost a
notification they would otherwise have received. But production state WAS changed by the probe, and it
demonstrates the finding: any anonymous caller can burn the outbox this way.

## 🔴 C-SQL-1 — `claim_token` lets any authenticated user overwrite ANOTHER user's `token_claim_history` row

**Severity:** Critical (live today — the mitigating check is behind a flag that is OFF)
**Latest definition:** `supabase/migrations/0060_batch_token_preclaim.sql:149-159` (verified: `claim_token`
is NOT redefined in any later migration).

**Verified code:**
```sql
INSERT INTO public.token_claim_history (token, user_id, ...)
VALUES (lower(p_token), v_uid, ...)
ON CONFLICT (token) DO UPDATE SET
  valid_until = EXCLUDED.valid_until,
  approx_lat  = COALESCE(EXCLUDED.approx_lat, public.token_claim_history.approx_lat),
  ...
```
There is **no `WHERE token_claim_history.user_id = v_uid`** on the `DO UPDATE`. The conflict target is the
token alone, but the security-relevant key is (token, owner).

**The `COALESCE` guard is dead code.** Its comment claims it will "never blank out a fix an earlier claim
wrote", but `0060:117-118` raises `'Fresh coordinates are required'` when `p_lat IS NULL`, so
`EXCLUDED.approx_lat` is *always* non-NULL and `COALESCE(non_null, existing)` always returns the caller's
value. Every conflicting call unconditionally overwrites the stored coordinates.

**Why the attacker has the token:** beacon tokens are broadcast in plaintext over BLE. Any modified client
harvests them passively from anyone in range.

**Consequence — the GPS veto is neutralised.** `correlate_encounter` (`0053:179-182`) vetoes an encounter
by comparing the caller's coordinates against `v_claim.approx_lat/lon`. Having just written that row
themselves, an attacker sets both sides equal and the distance is 0. The spatial half of the anti-forgery
envelope is removed, so a relay attack no longer needs to know where the victim is.

**Flag gating:** the batch-membership check at `0060:127-133` would close this, but it only raises when
`enforce_batch_tokens >= 1`, and that flag is **currently 0**. So this is live.

**Fix:** add `WHERE public.token_claim_history.user_id = v_uid` to the `DO UPDATE`, making a foreign-owned
conflict a silent no-op; and reject cross-owner claims even with the flag off.

**Confidence:** CERTAIN (read the latest definition; confirmed no later redefinition).

## 🔴 C-SQL-2 — `correlate_miles_encounters` fabricates encounters from arbitrary GPS, bypassing the entire 0029 reciprocity gate

**Severity:** Critical (live, not gated by any rollout flag)
**Latest definition:** `0048_gps_scope_and_retention.sql:251-360`. Entry point `record_location_ping`
(`0019:1159`) calls it at `:1227`. Grant: `0008_miles_correlation.sql:263` →
`GRANT EXECUTE ... TO authenticated, service_role`. **Verified: no later migration revokes it.**
`0061`'s privilege sweep revokes from `anon` only and explicitly preserves `authenticated`
(`0061:97-98`: "It revokes from anon only. authenticated is the legitimate client RPC surface").

**Verified code:** the function `INSERT`s directly into `public.encounters` for up to 100 peers per call,
setting `user_a, user_b, neighborhood, encounter_time, last_seen_at, range_type, confidence, status` —
and **no `trust_level`**. Compare `correlate_encounter` (`0053:208-209`), which sets `'mutual_ble'`.

**The 0029 reciprocal-confirmation gate applies ONLY to the BLE path.** There are two encounter producers
in this schema; one was hardened through 0029→0053 and the other was left at its original design. Caller
coordinates are validated only for numeric range and a 30-second dedupe — no plausibility check, no
impossible-travel check.

**Exploit:** call `record_location_ping(lat, lon, 'miles_10')` with any coordinates on Earth. That
synchronously creates `encounters` rows with every discoverable, preference-compatible, non-blocked user
who pinged within ~16 km. Repeat every 30s while teleporting the origin across a metro area. No GPS
hardware, no BLE, no physical presence.

**Second effect — a presence/identity oracle.** The function `RETURNS TABLE (encounter_id, other_user_id,
created_new)`, handing the caller raw `user_id`s of real users near an attacker-chosen point, unbucketed
and with no reveal delay.

**Fix:** stop this path writing `public.encounters` (give Locals its own table), or at minimum stamp
`trust_level='gps_only'` and exclude that value everywhere encounters are treated as evidence; stop
returning `other_user_id` to `authenticated`; add impossible-travel rejection in `record_location_ping`.

**Confidence:** CERTAIN.

## 🔴 C-SQL-3 — `beacon_token_batch` has NO scheduled purge: a permanent token→user_id map that de-anonymises 30 days of `rssi_samples`

**Severity:** Critical (privacy)

**Verified:** `cleanup_ephemeral_data()` — latest definition `0059_proximity_wake_producer.sql:477-580` —
purges 9 tables (`token_claims`, `sightings`, `location_pings`, `token_claim_history`, `rssi_samples`,
`venue_anchors`, `proximity_wake_requests`, `rssi_batch_rate`, `notification_outbox`).
**`beacon_token_batch` is not among them.**

Every `DELETE FROM public.beacon_token_batch` in the entire migration set is either
(a) self-scoped inside `issue_token_batch` (`0031:69`, `0034:105`) — runs only when *that same user*
next requests a batch, or (b) an account-deletion/scrub path (`0035:124`, `0037:172`, `0044:204`,
`0056:265`, `0058:119`, `0059:240`). There is **no retention-driven purge**.

**Why it is Critical:** `rssi_samples.correlation_id` and `beacon_token_batch.token` are the same value
space, so `JOIN beacon_token_batch b ON b.token = r.correlation_id` yields a fully de-anonymised
"who was physically near whom" graph at millisecond resolution, across the full 30-day `rssi_samples`
retention. The rotating token protects users from other users — not from the server or anyone with a
database copy. `0056:398-400` claims "the counterpart is a rotating correlation id, never a user id",
which is true of the column and false of the database.

A user who uninstalls or churns leaves their entire token set on the server permanently.

**Fix (two lines):** add
`DELETE FROM public.beacon_token_batch WHERE valid_until < NOW() - INTERVAL '24 hours';`
to `cleanup_ephemeral_data()`. The `idx_beacon_token_batch_expiry` index already exists for it.
This alone collapses the exposure from 30 days to 24 hours.

**Confidence:** CERTAIN.

## 🔴 C-CONSENT-1 — The three newest telemetry write paths have NO consent check at all

**Severity:** Critical (compliance — withdrawal is not effective)

**Verified:** `grep -n "require_consent\|consent_withdrawn"` over `0056_calibration_rssi_samples.sql`
and `0059_proximity_wake_producer.sql` returns **zero matches in either file**.

- `record_rssi_batch` (`0056:109`) checks auth, device-id length, JSON type, and a 500-row cap.
  No consent check of any purpose.
- `enqueue_proximity_wake` (`0059:116`) checks auth and a throttle. No consent check.
- `venue_anchors` has no RPC at all — the client writes the table directly under an RLS policy
  (`0057:60-65`), so there is no gate to bypass.

This is the same defect class the earlier audit fixed for `claim_token`/`record_sighting`, but worse:
that one checked the *wrong* purpose; these check *no* purpose.

**Fix:** add `require_consent(v_uid,'ble_proximity')` to `record_rssi_batch`,
`require_consent(v_uid,'precise_location')` to `enqueue_proximity_wake`, convert the `venue_anchors`
insert to a SECURITY DEFINER RPC with the same check, and add a `preciseLocation` branch to
`consent_screen.dart`'s withdrawal handler (it currently handles only `bleProximity` and
`photoProcessing`).

**Structural fix worth more than any of the above:** a pgTAP assertion that every RPC inserting into a
user-scoped table calls `require_consent`, plus a retention test that fails when a new table is added
without an entry in `cleanup_ephemeral_data`. Those two tests would have caught C-SQL-3 and
C-CONSENT-1 at authoring time. Both defects exist because these invariants are enforced by hand-applied
convention with nothing proving coverage.

**Confidence:** CERTAIN.

## 🔴 C-W5-1 — A committed encounter reached by `realId` bypasses the sticky-keeper branch; the keeper is silently displaced

**Severity:** Critical (reproduces the original #7 duplicate-keeper defect, no attacker required)
**Branch:** `fix/w5-encounter-lease`

**Verified structurally in BOTH implementations — the committed check precedes the `realId` lookup:**

| | committed branch | `realId` fallback |
|---|---|---|
| Dart `lib/features/beacon/w5_ownership.dart` | `:321` `if (e != null && e.committed) {` | `:351` `e ??= _enc[realId];` |
| Swift `ios/Runner/W5Ownership.swift` | `:250` `if let ec = e, ec.committed {` | `:279` `if e == nil { e = enc[realId] }` |

`e` at the committed check comes only from `_locate(peerAlias, myCandidate)` plus the `peerPrevAlias`
fallback. When the lease key is the **peer's** candidate (`peerCandidate < myCandidate`) and the incoming
`peerAlias` is not yet in `_aliasTo`, both lookups miss, the committed branch is skipped, and the
encounter is then picked up by `_enc[realId]` **as if it were a fresh negotiating encounter**.

**Executed proof (reviewer ran this against the Dart oracle):** committed encounter with keeper `p1`/`L5`;
a second `onControl` under a rotated (unknown) alias yields effects `[W5SendPropose]` — **no close of the
intruder, no `owns`** — and `committedKeeper` moves `p1 → p2`, `linkId` `L5 → L0`. The control probe using
the *known* alias correctly yields `[W5RejectInbound(p2)]` with the keeper unchanged, isolating the cause
to the `_locate` miss.

**This violates the design doc explicitly** (`docs/W5_ENCOUNTER_LEASE_DESIGN.md:295-296`):
"A committed keeper is sticky … a smaller-central intruder is closed without displacing the winner.
Committed leases never rekey."

**Production trigger — no attacker needed.** `W5LinkController.swift:104` mints the local candidate
per peer alias (`candidate(for: peerTokenHex)`). The peer rotates its ~15-minute token; `HELLO_ACK`
(`W5Codec.swift:50`) has **no `prevAlias` field at all**, and the outbound call site
(`W5LinkController.swift:208-211`) passes none — so on the outbound path a rotated peer alias is
unresolvable by construction. The inbound path (`:317`) does pass `peerPrevAlias`, which is why the
existing vector 2 is green and this stayed hidden.

**Consequence:** two live physical links to one peer, both kept alive; the adapter still holds `owns(p1)`
while the oracle reports `p2`, so the two endpoints can settle on **different** committed links — exactly
the #7 duplicate-keeper / double-counted-RSSI failure this state machine exists to prevent.

**Fix:** hoist the `realId` resolution above the committed check in both implementations (a two-line
change each), so a committed encounter always enters the sticky branch however it was located.
Belt-and-braces: have `committedKeeper`/`committedLinkId` return a winner *stored at commit* rather than
recomputing `winner()` from a mutable `links` map.

**Confidence:** CERTAIN (structure verified in both languages by direct read; behaviour executed in Dart).

---

## 🔴 C-W5-2 — Peripheral restoration permanently nils the notify characteristics: the peripheral can never send another control message

**Severity:** Critical
**File:** `ios/Runner/BackgroundBeacon.swift:736-751` (`willRestoreState`), `:714-734`, `:396-421`

`willRestoreState` sets `didRestorePeripheral = true` and `serviceAdded = true` but never re-binds
`controlNotifyChar` / `keepaliveNotifyChar` from the restored service's characteristics. Those objects are
created **only** inside `if !serviceAdded` in `reconfigureAdvertising`, so after a restoration relaunch
both stay `nil` for the entire process lifetime.

The device still advertises and still answers reads, so it looks healthy — but `notifyControl`
(`W5LinkController.swift:531-536`) returns early on every call. A central connects, subscribes, writes
HELLO, and we `respond(.success)` to the ATT write so it believes the write landed — while **the HELLO_ACK
is silently discarded**. Both endpoints stall permanently. Every `sendPropose`/`sendAck`/`sendReject` from
the peripheral role is dropped.

**Why this is the normal path, not an edge case:** for an app whose entire design is "iOS relaunches us
for BLE events", the restoration launch is the common case. Recovery requires a Bluetooth power cycle or a
non-restoration relaunch.

**Fix:** in `willRestoreState`, walk `svc.characteristics` and re-bind both references; set
`serviceAdded = false` (forcing a clean re-add) if either cannot be recovered.

**Confidence:** CERTAIN.

---

## 🔴 C-W5-3 — A dial that connects but dies before HELLO_ACK leaks a `pendingDial` forever: the encounter can never commit and can never be erased

**Severity:** Critical
**Files:** `ios/Runner/W5LinkController.swift:240-254`; `ios/Runner/W5Ownership.swift:516-530`, `:390-406`

Only `didFailToConnect` reaches `onDialFailed`. "Connected, then died before HELLO_ACK" arrives on
`didDisconnectPeripheral` → `linkDown` → `onLinkDown`, whose first act is
`handleTo.removeValue(forKey: handle)` — but the handle was never mapped (mapping happens in `onControl`,
which requires HELLO_ACK), so it returns `[]` immediately. `pendingDials` and `dialInFlight` survive.

Resulting permanent state for that peer: `maybeCommit` bails on `!e.pendingDials.isEmpty` so the encounter
**can never commit**; `onDiscovered` returns `[]` because `!e.inGrace` so we **never dial again**; and
nothing erases the lease (grace was never entered, `onDialFailed` never fires, `onTeardown` has no
production caller). If the peer later dials us, we broadcast an unmatchable PROPOSE **every 8 seconds for
the life of the encounter** while never committing — and because commit never happens, the loser-closing
never runs, which is issue #7 reopened silently for that pair.

The triggers are all mundane: peer walks out of range after `didConnect`; the 10s watchdog
(`BackgroundBeacon.swift:967-973`) cancels the connection without calling `dialFailed`; a CA6E decode
violation; a peer with no CA6E characteristic.

**Fix:** in `linkDown`/`closeOutboundLink`, branch on `link.established` — if false, feed
`onDialFailed(linkId:)` instead of `onLinkDown`. Add a TTL sweep for `pendingDials`.

**Confidence:** CERTAIN.

---

## 🔴 C-RT-1 — `_flushSightings` has no re-entrancy guard: one flush loop compounds per 45s on a slow network, and "turn beacon off" hangs for up to 83 minutes

**Severity:** Critical
**File:** `lib/features/beacon/beacon_service.dart:417-422`, `:2449-2483` (main)

The 45s periodic timer calls `_flushSightings()` without awaiting or guarding it. Each pass awaits up to
500 RPCs **sequentially at a 10s timeout** — ~83 minutes per pass on the half-dead-network condition this
same file documents twice ("with no/half-dead network this RPC *HANGS*"). The timer fires 111 more times
inside that window, each starting another full pass over the same still-populated queue. Loops grow
linearly with no ceiling.

Every sibling drain in this codebase IS guarded — `RssiUploader.flush` has `if (_busy) return`,
`_drainNativeBuffer` has `_nativeDrainInFlight`. The omission looks accidental.

**User-visible consequence:** `turnOffBeacon` awaits this flush (`:603`), holding `BeaconController._busy`.
**The user taps "off" and nothing happens for up to 83 minutes while BLE keeps running.**

**Fix:** add a `_flushInFlight` guard with a pending-fold, mirroring `_drainNativeBuffer`; bound the
per-pass record count; put a `.timeout()` on the flush inside `turnOffBeacon` so teardown can never be
held hostage by the network.

**Confidence:** CERTAIN (missing guard); LIKELY that this is a — possibly *the* — RH-1 wedge mechanism.
